name: ベーカリーカフェ SAN-HITORI（サン ヒトリ） (Bakery Cafe SAN-HITORI)

claims.text: This is a wheat-flour bakery where flour is handled throughout the small kitchen, so cross-contamination with gluten is unavoidable.
Dairy-based cream, eggs and meat items (such as fried chicken) are prepared in the same kitchen, so cross-contact for vegans is likely.
The entire menu centers on wheat noodles produced at the adjacent Harada Seimen factory, so the kitchen is a heavy wheat-flour environment.
The signature broth is described as intensely soy-sauce-forward; standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
Dishes are topped with pork chashu and served in a meat/fish-and-soy-based broth; no plant-only preparation is documented.

name: ブランジェリー 101ブリオ (Boulangerie 101 Brio)

claims.text: This is a working wheat-flour bakery; flour dust and shared surfaces make heavy gluten cross-contact unavoidable. Not appropriate for celiac or gluten-sensitive diners.
Breads and pastries are produced together using shared dough, ovens and equipment; dairy- and egg-containing items (cream pan, danishes) share the same production line as any plainer loaves.

name: カフェポンテ イタリアーノ (Caff'e Ponte ITALIANO)

claims.text: The kitchen runs a wood-fired pizza oven and fresh pasta service, so wheat flour is central to the cooking and gluten cross-contact should be assumed; no gluten-free handling is documented.
Dishes commonly use cheese, oysters, and fish-based sauces; no separate vegan preparation is described, so a vegan diner should confirm ingredients and shared cooking surfaces directly.
The restaurant advertises vegetarian options and provides menus in English, Chinese, and Korean, which makes it easier to discuss dietary needs.
Okonomiyaki and negiyaki are cooked on a single shared teppan griddle and built from wheat batter and wheat noodles, so heavy gluten cross-contact is unavoidable.
Dishes are finished with a wheat-based okonomiyaki/Worcestershire-style sauce, which contains wheat.
The shared griddle is used for pork, egg, seafood and oysters; specialties prominently feature egg, so vegan separation is not feasible.
Small two-person family operation cooking at the counter, so you can watch your dish made and speak directly with the cook about ingredients.

name: 中国料理 煌蘭苑 (Chugoku Ryori Kohranen)

claims.text: Cantonese-style Chinese cooking at this restaurant relies on standard Chinese seasonings such as soy sauce and oyster sauce, which contain wheat; no gluten-free preparation is documented.
The vegetarian course is lacto-ovo: it explicitly contains no meat or fish but does include dairy (a milk-based pudding) and eggs, so it is not vegan without modification.
A dedicated meat-and-fish-free vegetarian course is offered with a required reservation at least three days in advance, indicating the kitchen accommodates dietary requests arranged ahead of time.
Offers a dedicated vegetarian course and à la carte vegetarian items free of meat and fish, built on vegetables, mushrooms, tofu, and black sticky rice.

name: 中華料理 龍王 (Chuka Ryori Ryuoh)

claims.text: Standard Chinese kitchen frying spring rolls and serving wheat ramen alongside stir-fries; shared woks and fryers make cross-contact with wheat highly likely.
Dishes are seasoned in the typical machi-chuka style with soy sauce, which in Japan is wheat-based unless stated otherwise.
Menu is built around meat (liver, char siu pork, meat spring rolls) cooked on shared equipment; no vegan preparation is documented.

name: 中華そば くにまつ（國松） (Chuka Soba Kunimatsu)

claims.text: The dandan sauce is based on soy sauce and miso, which are wheat-containing; the noodles are wheat ramen noodles.
The dish is built on minced pork with egg toppings available, so vegan diners cannot be safely accommodated.
